text:
Samir: FYI saw a big regenerative cache flood hitting kv-proxy around 09:12 UTC. Lots of concurrent prefix backfills that cascaded into kernel-selection churn and CPU hot loops. Suspecting keying mismatch + new batching heuristic.

Jess: Oof. Any obvious trigger? rollout? model swap? :rotating_light:

Samir: No deployment in the hour before. We did flip a quantization kernel selector flag on a small % (demo rollout). Metric spike aligns with that flip + a sudden rise in prefix variety from one customer.

Ravi: Do we have the profiler traces? CPU flame shows many short-lived threads in the kernel picker path. I think the new selector is doing expensive fallback scoring per-request.

Maya: Pulling traces and sample logs now. Also seeing prefix key entropy jump: 95th pct prefix length increased and cache hit-rate dropped from 82% to 21% within 3m.

Samir: Paste of the key metric snapshot: ```
kv_cache.hit_rate: 0.82 -> 0.21
kv_proxy.pending_backfills: 0 -> 380
kernel.selector.latency_p50: 2ms -> 18ms
kernel.selector.fallback_count: +14k
cpu.user: +160%```

Jess: That pending_backfills number is the killer. If many requests concurrently miss, we push work to the backend and also trigger more kernel fallbacks -> amplification. This looks like a regenerative flood (not a single stampede origin).

Ravi: Agreed. Two-pronged mitigation suggested: (1) emergency backoff on kv-proxy that batches/reacts to high backfill queue (fast path: slow responses instead of triggering backfills); (2) rollback the kernel selector flag since the selector is amplifying cost per miss.

Maya: I started a canary rollback on the selector flag for 10% -> 0% (rollout API used). Will monitor. Also pushed a conservative kv-proxy config: backfill_rate_limit=25 and prefetch_coalesce_window=180ms.

infra-bot: deploy.start Samir rolled back kernel-selector-flag to 0% (job id: dpl-8891).

Jess: Nice. Can we also gate prefix keying normalization? The client-side keying variant for that customer looked different (added session tokens in prompt). We should normalise or strip ephemeral session fields server-side for cache keys.

Samir: Agreed. I created a short-term patch to strip long ephemeral tokens from cache keys for the next hour (kv-proxy transform). Patch: ``kvkey.normalize.strip_patterns=["session_token","uuidv4"]``. Rolling now.

Ravi: After the rollback + kv-proxy backoff, hit-rate recovered to ~68% within 7 minutes and pending_backfills down to ~12. Kernel selector latency back to baseline.

Maya: Logs show a distinct phase: initial miss flood -> aggressive selector scoring -> many small kernel fallbacks -> backend CPU spike -> proxy backfill queue growth. Sequence captured in profiling link: https://perf.redwood.local/traces/2143658700 (sample).

Jess: Follow-ups: 1) revert permanent selector change until we add cheap cache-awareness to selector (avoid per-request heavy scoring when backfill queue > threshold), 2) add a fast path in kv-proxy that returns stale cached prefix when backfill queue high (serve slightly stale vs. hammer backend), 3) add histogram of prefix-token-entropy to alerting.

Samir: Filed tickets: RW-ops-1421 (selector rollback + tests), RW-ops-1422 (kv-proxy backpressure fast-path), RW-ops-1423 (prefix-entropy alert). Assigning owners.

Oncall-Router: Incident annotated and status: mitigated. Root cause: aggressive kernel selector rollout + high-entropy client keying leading to massive cache misses and regenerative backfill amplification. Action items as above.

Ravi: We'll also add a micro-benchmark in CI that simulates high-prefix-entropy traffic with selector enabled to catch this earlier.

Maya: TL;DR: emergency rollback + kv-proxy backoff + key normalization fixed it. Will monitor the next 2 hours and then plan a safer selector rollout with cache-awareness. :white_check_mark:
